Gibbon himself explored ideas of internal decline and of attacks from outside the empire. Many historians have postulated reasons for the collapse of the Western Roman Empire, including a decline in "civic virtue" and military and economic capability. Modern scholarship has introduced additional factors such as climate change, epidemic diseases, and environmental degradation as important reasons for the decline.
